title: Midquarter reset talking points (scratch)
content:
Purpose: quick scratch for an all-hands-style 10–12 minute update (mid-quarter reset). Not polished — talking bullets, Qs, and quick metrics to pull.

Audience: whole company; tone: transparent, engineering-first, pragmatic. Emphasize tradeoffs, where we will invest, and what we expect from teams (focus).

Topline headline (1 sentence): We're tightening focus for the next 6–10 weeks to improve inference unit economics and reliability while maintaining momentum on Private deployments — this means short-term shifts in resourcing and a set of fast experiments we want every product/team to align with.

Key talking points (order for 10-minute slot):
- Why: customers are telling us margin sensitivity + reliability above all; our telemetry shows small tail of high-latency cohorts and model variants that drive cost.
- What we will do: three concentrated efforts (Optimize sprint, Reliability Sprint, Private ramp):
  - Optimize sprint (4–6 weeks): aggressive batching + cache experiments, quantization profiles per workload, RL-based routing pilot. Goal = 15–25% unit cost improvement on selected workloads.
  - Reliability Sprint (4 weeks): fix top 5 latency regressions, improve cold-start behavior, expand fallback policies to cover cross-region failover. Goal = hit 99.9% p99 for core hosted API routes.
  - Private ramp (ongoing): finalize onboarding flow and KMS integrations for 3 pilot customers; deliver simplified ops blueprint for Private installs.
- What it means for teams: prioritize roadmap items that unblock these three efforts. Pause longer-term exploratory projects that are not directly linked to cost/reliability or Private readiness.

Numbers to surface (choose 2–3):
- Current p50/p95/p99 for text-gen hosted: 60ms / 220ms / 1.4s (global average) — note: p99 driven by 3% of requests with >5s cold starts.
- Current hosted unit cost baseline: $0.011/token (weighted average across models). Target: 15% reduction on pilot workloads.
- Dedicated capacity utilization: 68% average, 90% during peaks for certain customers (shows headroom/opportunity).

Customer example (1 quick line):
- Pilot customer X saw unpredictable billing spikes that caused them to throttle features; our Optimize experiment in week 1 materially reduced their token spend on reranks by ~18% in a small A/B. (anonymized)

Anticipated tough questions and short answers (for CEO/VPs to use):
- Q: Will this mean layoffs or hiring freeze?
  - A: We do not plan company-wide layoffs. We are pausing select hires that are not mission-critical and prioritizing internal reassignments to the sprints. We may open targeted reqs to support Private pilots.
- Q: Why not keep all projects running in parallel?
  - A: Parallel work dilutes leverage. These three efforts have the clearest, measurable impact on revenue, churn, and margin.
- Q: How will success be measured?
  - A: Predefined metrics per sprint (unit-cost delta, p99 improvement, Private onboarding time). We'll publish a short scoreboard weekly.
- Q: Will product roadmaps shift?
  - A: Short-term yes; long-term roadmaps remain. Treat this as a tactical reset to de-risk the next big launches.

Operational notes / what I need to prep before talking:
- Get final numbers from Observability team: last 30 days p50/p95/p99 by route (assigned to Rhea).
- One-slide visuals: cost delta waterfall (Ava).
- Short customer quote (anonymized) from CS to illustrate urgency (ask Priya in CS).
- Update the public-facing status page with a brief note about reliability work (SRE to own).

Post-talk follow-ups (quick checklist):
- Publish a Confluence playbook with sprint charters + owners (me + Rhea).
- Create tracking tickets: JIRA board with swimlanes for Optimize, Reliability, Private.
- Weekly 30-minute cross-functional sync (Mon mornings) for the sprint reviews.

Talk cadence / script fragments (notes to self):
- Opening: 1–2 lines referencing customer feedback and the telemetry trend; set the "why".
- Middle: bullets on the three efforts, with 1 metric each.
- Close: what success looks like and next steps; invite questions and where to follow up.

Loose language for the talk (feel free to paraphrase):
- "We launched fast and learned fast. Now we need a short, sharp period of focus to ensure the economics and reliability scale with usage."
- "This is not a slowdown of ambition: it's choosing the highest-leverage bets so we can keep moving quickly without surprise billing or outages."

Open questions I still want to resolve (for myself):
- Are there any enterprise contracts that would be negatively impacted if we throttle certain bursty endpoints during experiments? (ask legal/sales)
- Can we commit to a public weekly scoreboard? storage/infra cost for longer retention? (ops + product)
- Do we need a separate comms thread for Dedicated customers about utilization/overprovisioning? (customer success)

Risks and mitigations (short):
- Risk: Perception that this is a cost-cutting exercise -> Mitigate: emphasize customer experience and runway for Private.
- Risk: Sprints pull too many key engineers off ongoing launches -> Mitigate: scoped ownership, temporary backfills, clear end dates.

Quick TODOs (today):
- Pull last 30-day p99 by route (Rhea).
- Draft 1-slide visuals + share with leadership (Ava).
- Share this scratch doc with Rhea + Ava and ask for edits.

Note to self: keep the talk <12 minutes. Leave 8–10 minutes for Q&A.

----
Scratchy, intentionally terse. Save as draft, iterate with Rhea/Ava.

End of scratch.
